title: Telemetry gateway, adaptive sampler, and context sanitization
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Problem: Our current telemetry pipeline has two issues: 1) under bursty traffic the tracer and metric flush paths add significant tail latency and memory pressure, and 2) context propagation occasionally surfaces internal metadata (long trace attributes and ephemeral binary blobs) into downstream exporters, increasing payload size and causing backend spikes. Goal: Introduce a lightweight telemetry gateway inside the runtime that centralizes batching/flush behavior, implement an adaptive sampling proxy to drop or downsample low-value spans/metrics, and add a deterministic context sanitizer to remove large or sensitive attributes before export. Success criteria: reduced 99th-percentile telemetry-related latency by >= 40% on the inference runtime, reduced average telemetry egress bytes by >= 30%, and no customer-visible loss of high-value traces (SLO: 99% of high-severity traces preserved).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Gateway correctly batches traces and metrics with configurable max-batch-size and max-latency; 2) Adaptive sampler keeps high-priority traces (error/latency anomalies/service-critical) and downsamples routine traces; 3) Context sanitizer removes attributes over size threshold and strips configured sensitive keys; 4) Load test demonstrates 40% reduction in telemetry tail latency and 30% reduction in egress bytes; 5) End-to-end compatibility with existing OTLP exporters and Palo/Datadog bridges; 6) Rolling rollout plan with feature flag and telemetry canary validating no increase in errors.
implementation_notes:
- Add a 'telemetry-gateway' service inside runtime process to handle batching and flow control rather than callers writing directly to exporters.
- Gateway provides two export paths: fast-path local aggregator and fallback remote exporter (async).
- Implement adaptive sampler using lightweight heuristic: priority score = error_flag*10 + latency_score + sampling_hint; use sliding window counters to compute downsample rates.
- Context sanitizer runs before batching; rules loaded from config center and allow regexp-based key stripping and size thresholds.
- Keep the instrumentation API unchanged; shim to ensure backward compatibility.
- Expose runtime metrics for gateway queue length, drop-rate, sanitized-attr-count, and egress-bytes.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature off by default in staging; run synthetic load tests. 2) Enable for internal smoke clusters behind feature flag + sampling ratio 0.01 for non-critical traces. 3) Gradually increase sampling for low-cost paths while keeping full sampling for errors and latency > threshold. 4) Monitor egress-bytes, telemetry-latency-99p, and customer error rates for 72h per stage. 5) Promote to production with a 7-day canary at 5% traffic, 25% and then 100% if metrics stable. 6) Automated rollback if telemetry-latency-99p increases > 10% or customer-visible error rate increases.
perf_targets:
- telemetry-e2e-99p-latency: reduce from 120ms to <= 72ms on typical runtime workloads (-40%).
- telemetry-egress-bytes-per-req: reduce by >= 30% on average.
- CPU overhead of gateway: <= 2% of runtime process CPU at steady state.
- Memory additional RSS: <= 60MB per runtime shard under peak load.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for adaptive sampler heuristics and sanitizer regex rules.
- Integration tests exercising batching thresholds and exporter fallback.
- Load tests in perf lab replaying production traces (use 24h trace replay).
- Chaos tests: introduce exporter latency and ensure gateway backpressure maintains runtime SLOs.
- End-to-end verification with Datadog and Prometheus exporters against test backends.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: Over-aggressive sampling drops important traces -> Mitigation: conservative default rules, prioritized traces are always preserved and we ship a sampling-override debug flag.
- Risk: Sanitizer accidentally removes required troubleshooting fields -> Mitigation: audit logs of removed keys and a reversible whitelist mode for first two weeks.
- Risk: Gateway adds CPU/memory cost -> Mitigation: profiling budget, opt for zero-copy buffers, use pool allocators and tunable concurrency.
- Risk: Interoperability with 3rd-party exporters -> Mitigation: keep OTLP wire format untouched and add compatibility suite for Datadog/Signoz/Prometheus exporters.
monitoring_and_alerting: New dashboards and alerts added: telemetry.gateway.queue_length, telemetry.gateway.flush_latency_99p, telemetry.gateway.drop_rate, telemetry.sanitizer.removed_attr_count, telemetry.egress_bytes_per_minute. Alerts: page if drop_rate > 2% sustained for 5m or egress_bytes change > +/-20% vs baseline.
deployment_notes:
- Deploy gateway behind feature flag; the config uses remote config; ops can toggle sampling thresholds per-cluster.
- Migration: turn on gateway in read-only (no-drop) mode for first day to collect baseline, then enable sanitizer and sampling progressively.
- Backwards compat: if gateway fails, runtime falls back to direct exporter writes (current behavior).
